problem: A client sends requests; it doesn't receive them. Nothing can call a user's browser or app like a server.
suggestion: Flip the cable so the client is the caller, or send the reply back along the same cable.

problem: Clients shouldn't talk to a database or cache directly: anyone could read or change everything, and every user would hold a connection open.
suggestion: Put an App Server (or an API Gateway in front of one) between the client and the data.

problem: Clients don't talk to background plumbing directly. It has no way to check who is asking or answer them.
suggestion: Send the client to an App Server, and let the server hand work to the queue.

problem: Databases, caches and monitoring tools answer or watch; they don't call your servers.
suggestion: Flip the cable so the server calls them instead.

problem: This sits in front of servers and passes requests on to them. Reaching a database straight from here skips the code that decides what to read or write.
suggestion: Connect it to an App Server, and the App Server to the data.

problem: A cache holds answers; it doesn't call servers.
suggestion: Flip the cable so the server checks the cache.
